one_liner: Hand-built CUDA-graph inference pipelines for robot VLA models (Pi0/Pi0.5, GR00T) on Jetson Thor and RTX GPUs; beats TensorRT latency.
what_it_does: FlashRT is a batch-1, latency-first inference engine for a fixed set of models: vision-language-action policies (Pi0, Pi0.5, Pi0-FAST, GR00T N1.6/N1.7, LingBot), plus some LLM, VLM, TTS and video paths. You call flash_rt.load_model(checkpoint, config='pi05', framework='torch' or 'jax').predict(images, prompt); it loads safetensors or Orbax checkpoints directly, with no ONNX export or engine build, and picks a Thor, RTX 5090 or RTX 4090 backend from the GPU's compute capability. A C ABI (frt_model_runtime_v1) and a native C++ Pi0.5 path exist for Python-free deployment, and the separate FlashRT-Structures package attaches its kernels to unmodified PyTorch hosts.
how_it_is_fast: Each model's whole forward pass (vision encoder, LLM backbone and the 4-step diffusion action head) is written out by hand and captured once as a static CUDA Graph over fixed buffers, so steady-state calls are a graph replay with no Python dispatch. Activations and weights run in static per-tensor FP8 (E4M3), or NVFP4 with AWQ pre-scaling on Blackwell, calibrated on the first call and cached as JSON. Hand-written CUDA kernels fuse the memory-bound steps (residual + RMSNorm + quantize, bias + GELU + quantize, RoPE/QKV split), while GEMMs and attention go to cuBLASLt FP8 with epilogue fusion, CUTLASS and a vendored FlashAttention-2 (FA4 or CUTLASS FMHA on Thor).
when_to_use: Closed-loop robot control with Pi0/Pi0.5/GR00T on Jetson AGX Thor: Pi0.5 2-view 44 ms FP8 (27 ms NVFP4) vs 91-95 ms for NVIDIA's TensorRT baseline
Batch-1 VLA inference on RTX 5090/4090 where per-decision latency matters more than throughput (GR00T N1.6 2-view about 13 ms graph replay)
You want to skip TensorRT engine builds, per-driver/per-GPU rebuilds and ONNX export; a model change only needs a process restart
Fixed-architecture realtime workloads it already supports (Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4 single-stream decode, Higgs Audio TTS, Wan2.2/Cosmos video) on Blackwell
when_not_to_use: Multi-user or high-batch serving: one process serves one captured graph, with no continuous batching (the docs point to vLLM/SGLang/TRT-LLM)
Models it does not ship: each new architecture needs an 800-1500 line hand-written frontend and weight spec, not an automatic import

When you need FP32/BF16-exact outputs: the fast tiers are FP8/NVFP4 with about 0.998-0.999 action cosine to the reference, and 1-view NVFP4 Pi0.5 misses the project's own 0.995 gate (worst sample 0.971)
When you need a published number reproduced exactly: open issues report 21.24 ms vs a documented 16.61 ms (GR00T N1.7, RTX 5090, #188) and 25.76 vs 42.8 tok/s (Qwen3.6 on Thor, #153)
GPUs older than SM80, or Hopper if you need FlashAttention (FA2 is not built for sm90, which falls back to cuBLAS-decomposed attention)

integration.dependencies: CUDA 12.4+ (12.8+ for Blackwell), PyTorch or pinned JAX 0.5.3, pybind11, CUTLASS v4.4.2 (cloned into third_party), transformers<4.56, safetensors, numpy; vendored FlashAttention-2 v2.7.4.post1 built in; ROCm/hipBLASLt for the separate MI350X backend
integration.min_toolchain: C++17/CUDA C++17, GCC 11+, CMake 3.24+, Python 3.10-3.12; built with -O3 --use_fast_math
integration.platforms: NVIDIA SM80+ Linux: Jetson AGX Thor (SM110), RTX 5090 (SM120), DGX Spark (SM121), RTX 4090 (SM89), A100/RTX 3090, Jetson Orin (community port); AMD MI350X (gfx950) via a separate HIP backend
integration.thread_safety: not documented; one model per process (the Thor troubleshooting table says to subprocess-isolate rather than load several VLA checkpoints in one process)

gotchas: The RTX 5090 figures (GR00T N1.6 13.08 ms, Pi0.5 17.58 ms) are CUDA-graph replay p50 that exclude image normalization, host-device copies and post-processing; Pi0.5 wall-clock p50 is 19.58 ms at 2 views
GR00T 'T=50' is the action horizon, not the denoising step count; FlashRT's GR00T DiT also runs 4 steps, the same count as NVIDIA's table
CUDA Graph instantiation on Thor varies by about 2 ms run to run; autotune=3 (default) recaptures, and Pi0.5 NVFP4 needs about 300 warmup calls to settle

pip install flash-rt ships no compiled kernels; load_model needs an editable install plus a 6-25 minute CMake build with the same Python interpreter; the GR00T base checkpoint emits noise for untrained embodiment slots (use gr1 etc.)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick FlashRT for batch-1 robot policy (VLA) inference on Jetson Thor or RTX Blackwell; for LLM serving pick FlashInfer- or ZhiLight-style engines (or vLLM/SGLang), and for general transformer encoders and translation pick FasterTransformer or CTranslate2, which cover many architectures without a hand-written pipeline per model.
verified_claims_summary: FlashRT's own FP8 latencies for GR00T-N1.6-3B (Thor 45 ms end to end; RTX 5090 13.08 ms graph replay) are set against NVIDIA's published GR00T-N1.6 TensorRT, torch.compile and eager numbers (92/105/117 ms Thor, 31/37/58 ms RTX 5090), not re-measured in one harness; the only matched-harness rows (GR00T N1.7 LIBERO on Thor, JetPack 7.2 MAXN, 4 denoising steps, batch 1, medians of 20 runs) show 36.8 ms FP8 vs TensorRT FP8 ~44 ms and 23.7 ms NVFP4 vs TensorRT mixed NVFP4 ~40 ms (about 1.2x and 1.7x). Kernels are built with -O3 --use_fast_math; the CUDA toolkit used per row is not stated.
status_note: Very active, young (2026) Apache-2.0 project with frequent releases and community ports (Orin, L40, MI350X), but open, unanswered reproduction disputes (#188, #153) mean you should benchmark it yourself before relying on the headline numbers.
